requirements.quote: Clients are allowed to send further Control Packets immediately after sending a CONNECT Packet; Clients need not wait for a CONNACK Packet to arrive from the Server.
requirements.condition: After a Client sends CONNECT and before it receives CONNACK
requirements.required_behavior: The Client is permitted to send further Control Packets immediately without waiting for CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: A Client can be observed sending a second Control Packet while the Server deliberately delays CONNACK.

requirements.quote: If the Server rejects the CONNECT, it MUST NOT process any data sent by the Client after the CONNECT Packet [MQTT-3.1.4-5].
requirements.condition: When the Server rejects a CONNECT Packet
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must leave all later Client data following that CONNECT unprocessed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not process any data sent by the Client after the rejected CONNECT Packet.
requirements.error_behavior: Discard or otherwise leave unprocessed all post-CONNECT Client data associated with the rejected connection attempt.
requirements.why_checkable: Data can be pipelined after a CONNECT that the Server rejects, and side effects or responses can be monitored.

requirements.quote: The CONNACK Packet is the packet sent by the Server in response to a CONNECT Packet received from a Client.
requirements.condition: When a CONNACK Packet is sent
requirements.required_behavior: It must be sent by the Server to the Client as the response to that Client's CONNECT Packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A Client must not send CONNACK, and CONNACK must not be used as a response to a different Control Packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet direction and the immediately preceding connection request can be captured and correlated.

requirements.quote: The first packet sent from the Server to the Client MUST be a CONNACK Packet [MQTT-3.2.0-1].
requirements.condition: When the Server sends its first MQTT Control Packet to a newly connecting Client
requirements.required_behavior: That first Server-to-Client packet must be CONNACK.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not send another MQTT Control Packet type before CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection trace can identify and decode the first Server-to-Client Control Packet.

requirements.quote: If the Client does not receive a CONNACK Packet from the Server within a reasonable amount of time, the Client SHOULD close the Network Connection. A "reasonable" amount of time depends on the type of application and the communications infrastructure.
requirements.condition: When CONNACK is not received within a reasonable amount of time
requirements.required_behavior: The Client should close the Network Connection.
requirements.error_behavior: Close the Network Connection after the timeout.
requirements.why_checkable: The timeout threshold is deliberately application- and infrastructure-dependent and no observable numeric boundary is supplied in this chunk.

requirements.quote:
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 1	MQTT Control Packet Type (2)	Reserved
	0	0	1	0	0	0	0	0
requirements.condition: For a CONNACK Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Bits 7 through 4 of fixed-header byte 1 must encode MQTT Control Packet type 2 as 0010.
requirements.why_checkable: The high nibble of the first CONNACK byte can be compared directly with 0010.

requirements.quote:
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 1	MQTT Control Packet Type (2)	Reserved
	0	0	1	0	0	0	0	0
requirements.condition: For a CONNACK Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Reserved bits 3 through 0 of fixed-header byte 1 must be 0000.
requirements.why_checkable: The low nibble of the first CONNACK byte can be masked and compared with zero.

requirements.quote:
byte 2	Remaining Length (2)
	0	0	0	0	0	0	1	0
requirements.condition: For a CONNACK Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Fixed-header byte 2 must encode Remaining Length as 2 (0x02).
requirements.why_checkable: The second CONNACK byte can be compared directly with 0x02.

requirements.quote: This is the length of the variable header.
requirements.condition: When computing Remaining Length for CONNACK
requirements.required_behavior: Remaining Length must equal the byte length of the CONNACK variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded variable-header byte count can be compared with the Remaining Length value.

requirements.quote: For the CONNACK Packet this has the value 2.
requirements.condition: For the CONNACK Remaining Length field
requirements.required_behavior: The value must be exactly 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded numeric Remaining Length can be asserted as two.

requirements.quote:
Connect Acknowledge Flags	Reserved	SP1
byte 1		0	0	0	0	0	0	0	X
requirements.condition: For the CONNACK variable header
requirements.required_behavior: Connect Acknowledge Flags must occupy byte 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The first variable-header byte can be decoded as the Connect Acknowledge Flags field.

requirements.quote:
Connect Return code
byte 2		X	X	X	X	X	X	X	X
requirements.condition: For the CONNACK variable header
requirements.required_behavior: Connect Return code must occupy byte 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The second variable-header byte can be decoded as the Connect Return code field.

requirements.quote: Byte 1 is the "Connect Acknowledge Flags". Bits 7-1 are reserved and MUST be set to 0.
requirements.condition: For the CONNACK Connect Acknowledge Flags byte
requirements.required_behavior: Reserved bits 7 through 1 must all be zero.
requirements.why_checkable: The flags byte can be masked with 0xFE and compared with zero.

requirements.quote: Bit 0 (SP1) is the Session Present Flag.
requirements.condition: For the CONNACK Connect Acknowledge Flags byte
requirements.required_behavior: Bit 0 must encode Session Present.
requirements.why_checkable: The field position can be asserted by masking bit 0 of the flags byte.

requirements.quote: If the Server accepts a connection with CleanSession set to 1, the Server MUST set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet in addition to setting a zero return code in the CONNACK packet [MQTT-3.2.2-1].
requirements.condition: When the Server accepts a connection whose CONNECT has CleanSession set to 1
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must set Session Present to 0 in CONNACK.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not report an existing Session for an accepted CleanSession=1 connection.
requirements.why_checkable: An accepted CleanSession=1 CONNECT can be followed by decoding bit 0 of CONNACK flags.

requirements.quote: If the Server accepts a connection with CleanSession set to 1, the Server MUST set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet in addition to setting a zero return code in the CONNACK packet [MQTT-3.2.2-1].
requirements.condition: When the Server accepts a connection whose CONNECT has CleanSession set to 1
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must set the CONNACK Connect Return code to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The return-code byte can be decoded alongside the accepted CleanSession=1 response.

requirements.quote: If the Server has stored Session state, it MUST set Session Present to 1 in the CONNACK packet [MQTT-3.2.2-2].
requirements.condition: When CleanSession is 0 and the Server has stored Session state for the supplied client ID
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must set Session Present to 1 in CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: Stored state can be prepared for a client ID and the subsequent CONNACK flag observed.

requirements.quote: If the Server does not have stored Session state, it MUST set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet.
requirements.condition: When CleanSession is 0 and the Server has no stored Session state for the supplied client ID
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must set Session Present to 0 in CONNACK.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not claim stored Session state that does not exist.
requirements.why_checkable: A new client ID can connect with CleanSession=0 and the CONNACK flag decoded.

requirements.quote: This is in addition to setting a zero return code in the CONNACK packet [MQTT-3.2.2-3].
requirements.condition: When CleanSession is 0, no stored Session state exists, and the Server accepts the connection
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must set the CONNACK Connect Return code to 0 in addition to Session Present 0.
requirements.why_checkable: Both CONNACK variable-header bytes can be decoded for the no-stored-state acceptance branch.

requirements.quote: In the event that the value of Session Present received by the Client from the Server is not as expected, the Client can choose whether to proceed with the Session or to disconnect.
requirements.condition: When the Client receives an unexpected Session Present value
requirements.required_behavior: The Client is permitted either to proceed with the Session or to disconnect.
requirements.error_behavior: Proceed or disconnect according to the Client's chosen recovery policy.
requirements.why_checkable: An unexpected flag can be injected and either stated outcome observed without treating the selected branch as nonconformant.

requirements.quote: The Client can discard the Session state on both Client and Server by disconnecting, connecting with Clean Session set to 1 and then disconnecting again.
requirements.condition: When a Client chooses to discard Session state on both endpoints
requirements.required_behavior: The Client may disconnect, reconnect with Clean Session set to 1, and then disconnect again in that order to discard both Client and Server Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: The three connection actions can be traced in order and Session-state absence checked afterward.

requirements.quote: If a server sends a CONNACK packet containing a non-zero return code it MUST set Session Present to 0 [MQTT-3.2.2-4].
requirements.condition: When CONNACK contains a nonzero Connect Return code
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must set Session Present to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A refusal CONNACK must not claim that a Session is present.
requirements.why_checkable: The return-code byte and Session Present bit can be decoded and cross-checked in one CONNACK.

requirements.quote: The values for the one byte unsigned Connect Return code field are listed in Table 3.1 – Connect Return code values.
requirements.condition: For the CONNACK Connect Return code field
requirements.required_behavior: The field must be encoded as one unsigned byte.
requirements.why_checkable: The variable header can be checked for exactly one byte at the return-code position and interpreted as unsigned.

requirements.quote: 0	0x00 Connection Accepted	Connection accepted
requirements.condition: When the Server accepts the connection
requirements.required_behavior: The CONNACK Connect Return code must be 0x00, meaning Connection Accepted.
requirements.why_checkable: The acceptance outcome can be correlated with the exact return-code byte.

requirements.quote: 1	0x01 Connection Refused, unacceptable protocol version	The Server does not support the level of the MQTT protocol requested by the Client
requirements.condition: When the Server refuses because it does not support the requested MQTT protocol level
requirements.required_behavior: The CONNACK Connect Return code must be 0x01, meaning unacceptable protocol version.
requirements.why_checkable: An unsupported protocol level can be sent and the returned byte compared with 0x01.

requirements.quote: 2	0x02 Connection Refused, identifier rejected	The Client identifier is correct UTF-8 but not allowed by the Server
requirements.condition: When the Client identifier is valid UTF-8 but is not allowed by the Server
requirements.required_behavior: The CONNACK Connect Return code must be 0x02, meaning identifier rejected.
requirements.why_checkable: A policy-rejected, well-encoded identifier can be supplied and the returned byte compared with 0x02.

requirements.quote: 3	0x03 Connection Refused, Server unavailable	The Network Connection has been made but the MQTT service is unavailable
requirements.condition: When the Network Connection exists but the MQTT service is unavailable
requirements.required_behavior: The CONNACK Connect Return code must be 0x03, meaning Server unavailable.
requirements.why_checkable: Server unavailability can be induced after transport connection and the returned byte compared with 0x03.

requirements.quote: 4	0x04 Connection Refused, bad user name or password	The data in the user name or password is malformed
requirements.condition: When the user name or password data is malformed
requirements.required_behavior: The CONNACK Connect Return code must be 0x04, meaning bad user name or password.
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed credential data can be supplied and the returned byte compared with 0x04.

requirements.quote: 5	0x05 Connection Refused, not authorized	The Client is not authorized to connect
requirements.condition: When the Client is not authorized to connect
requirements.required_behavior: The CONNACK Connect Return code must be 0x05, meaning not authorized.
requirements.why_checkable: An unauthorized Client can attempt connection and the returned byte compared with 0x05.

requirements.quote: 6-255		Reserved for future use
requirements.condition: For Connect Return code byte values 0x06 through 0xFF
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation must leave values 0x06 through 0xFF reserved for future use.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not send those values as MQTT 3.1.1 Connect Return codes, and a decoder must not assign them a current MQTT 3.1.1 meaning.
requirements.why_checkable: Serializer and decoder tables can be inspected or exercised across the reserved numeric range.

requirements.quote: If a well formed CONNECT Packet is received by the Server, but the Server is unable to process it for some reason, then the Server SHOULD attempt to send a CONNACK packet containing the appropriate non-zero Connect return code from this table.
requirements.condition: When a well-formed CONNECT is received but the Server cannot process it and a table return code applies
requirements.required_behavior: The Server should attempt to send CONNACK with the appropriate nonzero Connect Return code from Table 3.1.
requirements.error_behavior: Attempt an error CONNACK using the return code matching the failure reason.
requirements.why_checkable: Each listed failure reason can be induced and any attempted CONNACK decoded for the matching nonzero code.

requirements.quote: If a server sends a CONNACK packet containing a non-zero return code it MUST then close the Network Connection [MQTT-3.2.2-5].
requirements.condition: After the Server sends CONNACK with a nonzero Connect Return code
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must close the Network Connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not leave the refused MQTT connection open.
requirements.error_behavior: Close the Network Connection after the refusal CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: The refusal packet and subsequent transport closure can be observed in sequence.

requirements.quote: If none of the return codes listed in Table 3.1 – Connect Return code values are deemed applicable, then the Server MUST close the Network Connection without sending a CONNACK [MQTT-3.2.2-6].
requirements.condition: When no Table 3.1 Connect Return code applies to the connection failure
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must close the Network Connection.
requirements.why_checkable: An unrepresented failure can be induced and transport closure observed.

requirements.quote: If none of the return codes listed in Table 3.1 – Connect Return code values are deemed applicable, then the Server MUST close the Network Connection without sending a CONNACK [MQTT-3.2.2-6].
requirements.condition: When no Table 3.1 Connect Return code applies to the connection failure
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must close the connection without emitting CONNACK.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The Server must not send a CONNACK for that failure.
requirements.error_behavior: Suppress CONNACK and close the Network Connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet trace can be checked for absence of CONNACK before connection closure.

requirements.quote: The CONNACK Packet has no payload.
requirements.condition: For every CONNACK Packet
requirements.required_behavior: The packet must contain no payload bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A CONNACK Packet must not carry a payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The packet boundary and two-byte variable header permit a direct assertion that zero bytes remain as payload.

requirements.quote: A PUBLISH Control Packet is sent from a Client to a Server or from Server to a Client to transport an Application Message.
requirements.condition: When a PUBLISH Control Packet is transmitted
requirements.required_behavior: Its direction must be Client-to-Server or Server-to-Client.
requirements.why_checkable: Endpoint roles and packet direction can be observed on the Network Connection.

requirements.quote: A PUBLISH Control Packet is sent from a Client to a Server or from Server to a Client to transport an Application Message.
requirements.condition: When MQTT transports an Application Message using a PUBLISH Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: The PUBLISH Packet must carry the Application Message.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded PUBLISH contents can be correlated with the transported Application Message.

requirements.quote:
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 1	MQTT Control Packet type (3)	DUP flag	QoS level	RETAIN
	0	0	1	1	X	X	X	X
requirements.condition: For a PUBLISH Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: Bits 7 through 4 of fixed-header byte 1 must encode MQTT Control Packet type 3 as 0011.
requirements.why_checkable: The high nibble of the first PUBLISH byte can be compared directly with 0011.

requirements.quote: Position: byte 1, bit 3.
requirements.condition: For a PUBLISH Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: DUP must occupy fixed-header byte 1 bit 3.
requirements.why_checkable: A bit-mask check can confirm the DUP field's byte and bit position.

requirements.quote:
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 1	MQTT Control Packet type (3)	DUP flag	QoS level	RETAIN
	0	0	1	1	X	X	X	X
requirements.condition: For fixed-header byte 1 of a PUBLISH Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: QoS level must occupy bits 2 and 1 as a two-bit field.
requirements.why_checkable: A two-bit mask can confirm the position and width of the QoS field.

requirements.quote:
Bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0
byte 1	MQTT Control Packet type (3)	DUP flag	QoS level	RETAIN
	0	0	1	1	X	X	X	X
requirements.condition: For fixed-header byte 1 of a PUBLISH Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: RETAIN must occupy bit 0.
requirements.why_checkable: A bit-mask check can confirm the RETAIN field occupies bit 0.

requirements.quote: byte 2	Remaining Length
requirements.condition: For a PUBLISH Control Packet
requirements.required_behavior: The Remaining Length field must begin at fixed-header byte 2.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoder can assert the starting byte of Remaining Length in the PUBLISH fixed header.

requirements.quote: If the DUP flag is set to 0, it indicates that this is the first occasion that the Client or Server has attempted to send this MQTT PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.condition: When a PUBLISH Packet has DUP set to 0
requirements.required_behavior: The packet must be interpreted as the sender's first attempt to send that PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Sender attempt history can be correlated with the decoded DUP bit.

requirements.quote: If the DUP flag is set to 1, it indicates that this might be re-delivery of an earlier attempt to send the Packet.
requirements.condition: When a PUBLISH Packet has DUP set to 1
requirements.required_behavior: The receiver must interpret the packet as a possible re-delivery of an earlier send attempt.
requirements.why_checkable: A receiver's duplicate-handling path can be exercised using PUBLISH packets whose DUP bit is one.

requirements.quote: The DUP flag MUST be set to 1 by the Client or Server when it attempts to re-deliver a PUBLISH Packet [MQTT-3.3.1.-1].
requirements.condition: When a Client or Server attempts to re-deliver a PUBLISH Packet
requirements.required_behavior: The sender must set DUP to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The sender must not mark a re-delivery with DUP 0.
requirements.why_checkable: A forced re-delivery can be captured and the DUP bit decoded.

requirements.quote: The DUP flag MUST be set to 0 for all QoS 0 messages [MQTT-3.3.1-2].
requirements.condition: For every QoS 0 PUBLISH message
requirements.required_behavior: The sender must set DUP to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A QoS 0 PUBLISH message must not have DUP set to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The QoS bits and DUP bit can be decoded and cross-checked in each QoS 0 PUBLISH fixed header.
